verses.commentary: The word of the Lord came a second time. Grace repeats the call. God does not find a new prophet; he restores the old one. Second chances define the gospel. Jonah's failure did not disqualify him permanently.
Go to Nineveh. Same city. Same mission. Proclaim the message I give you. Not Jonah's message but God's. The prophet is a mouthpiece, not an author. Obedience means speaking what is given.

Jonah obeyed. Three words covering what chapter one refused to do. The belly of the fish was effective. Nineveh was exceedingly great, a three days' walk. Massive metropolis by ancient standards. The task looms large.

Forty more days and Nineveh will be overthrown. Five words in Hebrew. The shortest, most reluctant sermon ever preached. No call to repentance, no offer of mercy, just doom. Yet God uses even grudging obedience.

The Ninevites believed God. Immediate, massive response. No arguments, no delay. From the greatest to the least. Universal repentance. Sackcloth and fasting. What Israel refused for centuries, Assyria does in days.

The king rose from his throne. Removed his robes, put on sackcloth, sat in dust. Royal humiliation. The most powerful man in the known world humbles himself before the Hebrew God. Power recognizes greater power.
By decree of the king and his nobles. Official state repentance. Even animals must fast. Hyperbole? Perhaps. But it shows the totality of the response. The whole creation groans together.

Let everyone call urgently on God. Let them give up their evil ways and violence. Repentance is not just feeling but turning. Not just ritual but moral change. Violence was Assyria's trademark; now they renounce it.
Who knows? The king hopes but does not presume. God may relent. Beautiful humility. He makes no demands, claims no rights. Pure casting of self on divine mercy. This is the posture of faith.

When God saw what they did. Not just heard their words but saw their turning. God relented. The same word used of Jonah's wish that God not relent. Nineveh's repentance moves God's heart. Judgment threatened becomes mercy extended. The book's scandal: God's mercy has no boundaries.
